blocks.text:
After sailing overnight, the yacht reaches Isabela's west coast. This is the largest and youngest island in the archipelago, formed by 5 relatively young volcanoes. Giant tortoises and marine iguanas live here.

In the morning, you head to Punta Moreno. The trail passes through mangroves and basalt lava fields created by a major lava flow from Cerro Azul volcano hundreds of years ago. Mangrove lagoons line the coast, while small saltwater lagoons lie further inland. Here you can observe ducks, shorebirds, stilts, blue-winged teal and flamingos.

After the walk, you can snorkel near the shore or return to the yacht to relax with views of Isabela.

In the afternoon, the vessel heads north to the 6-kilometre Urbina Bay. This area was once underwater, but in 1954 it rose about 3 metres above sea level. Tortoises, land iguanas and the largest marine iguanas in the archipelago can be found here.

The day ends with dinner overlooking Isabela's 5 volcanoes. The menu includes seafood salad, baked fish, potato llapingachos, tuna crudo, grilled plantains and shrimp ceviche.
